einzeiler: How a failed baseball hopeful became a key player in the global arms trade.
kurzfassung: Will Summarandike transitioned from a failed brokerage career and minor league baseball dreams to building Regulus Global, a major private arms supplier. Leveraging Cold War stockpiles and speed, his company supplied weapons for covert US operations in Syria and Yemen, and later scaled up multi-billion dollar artillery shell deliveries for Ukraine. Despite facing regulatory setbacks, legal disputes, and shifting geopolitical landscapes, Summarandike continues to expand his influence through advanced ammunition manufacturing ventures.
stichpunkte: Will Summarandike transitioned from Wall Street cold-caller and aspiring baseball player to founding the defense contractor Regulus Global.
Regulus started by selling surplus military gear from a warehouse before moving into sourcing Soviet-era weapons for Pentagon-backed covert programs.
The company supplied ammunition for conflicts in Syria and Yemen, navigating complex international regulations and shadow supply chains.
Following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Summarandike secured major multi-billion dollar contracts to deliver critical 155mm artillery shells.
Regulus acquired state-owned arms factories in Bosnia to boost production, leading to a financial and legal dispute with Ukrainian state agencies over advance payments.
Summarandike launched Union, a venture-backed defense manufacturer in Texas aimed at applying modern automated manufacturing techniques to shell production.

beschreibung:
In this special bonus episode from The Financial Times, "The Broker" tells the story of how a failed baseball hopeful and disgraced stockbroker reinvented himself as one of America’s most consequential modern arms dealers.
From a family-run warehouse in Virginia Beach, Will Somerindyke built his company into a crucial conduit in the Pentagon’s covert supply chains — sourcing Soviet-era weapons for wars in Syria and Yemen before emerging as a central player in Ukraine’s fight against Russia.
As artillery shells became the most sought-after commodity of the war, he placed a multimillion-dollar bet on reviving crumbling Cold War factories in the Balkans, transforming himself from middleman to manufacturer.
Based on months of reporting, The Broker traces Somerindyke’s rise through the shadow world of privatized warfare — where geopolitics, profit and personal ambition collide — and reveals how modern conflicts are sustained not only by soldiers on the front lines, but by entrepreneurs who move the weapons behind the scenes.
This piece, written by the FT’s Miles Johnson, host of Hot Money Season 2: The New Narcos, was originally printed in FT Weekend.
